rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21 - statewide rent increase cap (struck from November 2026 ballot)
rules.requirement: Proposed ballot initiative that would have repealed the statewide ban on rent control and capped annual rent increases statewide at the lesser of CPI increase or 5% for most residential rental units. The SJC ruled in Cella v. Attorney General (SJC-13893) that it cannot appear on the November 2026 ballot because its religious-facility exemption makes it relate to religion under Article 48.
rules.key_value: Annual increase capped at lesser of CPI increase or 5%

new_construction_exemption.basis: newly constructed units less than 10 years old

unverifiable_exemptions: dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes
coverage.summary: Most residential rental units statewide, with exemptions for owner-occupied buildings of four or fewer units, units under 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and facilities operated solely for educational, religious or nonprofit purposes.
coverage.owner_conditions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units exempt

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units; newly constructed units less than 10 years old; certain publicly regulated units; short-term rentals; dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes.
rules.effective_date_note: Never took effect; the SJC held the petition may not appear on the November 2026 ballot.
citation_aliases: An Initiative Petition to Protect Tenants by Limiting Rent Increases
rules.quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%.
rules.review_note: Secondary source (law-firm blog). Backers reportedly may re-file without the religious exemption.

no_rule_findings.finding: Massachusetts currently has a statutory ban on rent control (G.L. c. 40P), which the failed petition would have repealed. The blog describes it as the existing ban, with no further text.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The petition would have repealed the Commonwealth’s existing statutory ban on rent control, G.L. c. 40P, and replaced it with a statewide cap on annual rent increases for most residential rental units.

result.doc_summary: Law-firm blog post reporting that the Massachusetts SJC, in Cella v. Attorney General (SJC-13893), held that Initiative Petition 25-21 (a statewide rent increase cap of the lesser of CPI or 5%) cannot appear on the November 2026 ballot because its religious-facility exemption violates Article 48's exclusion of measures relating to religion. The existing state ban on rent control (G.L. c. 40P) remains in place.
